status_summary: Recruiter access and Junior ROTC are addressed in law; the ASVAB requirement is not. The FY2025 NDAA (P.L. 118-159, Sec. 533) had already added a campus-access requirement for military recruiters on the same terms as other employers to the Elementary and Secondary Education Act, effective 2025-12-23. S. 3052 (introduced 2025-10-23) would have required equal campus access, at least four recruitment events a year on request, and student contact information. Public Law 119-60, the FY2026 NDAA enacted 2025-12-18, contains Sec. 531, which (per the U.S. Code notes) requires recruiter access equivalent to that of employers and colleges, at least one in-person event a year on request, and student contact data within 30 days, and Sec. 542, which raises the required Junior ROTC unit range from 3,400 to 4,000 to 3,600 to 4,200 effective 2027-10-01 and repeals an earlier 3,500 to 4,100 range that never took effect. A Senate committee chairman's release of 2026-05-05 says DOD directed an increase in Junior ROTC programs and delegated authority to set unit numbers to the Under Secretary for Personnel and Readiness, and CRS counted 3,475 units in FY2025. Neither section mentions the ASVAB, and no requirement that all students in federally funded schools take it was found.

timeline.event: S. 3052 introduced to require schools to give military recruiters the same campus access as other prospective employers, at least four in-person recruitment events a year on request, and student contact information.

President signs the FY2026 NDAA (P.L. 119-60). Per the U.S. Code amendment notes, Sec. 531 rewrites 10 U.S.C. 503(c)(1)(A) so that local educational agencies give military recruiters campus access equivalent to that given to prospective employers, colleges or other recruiters, at least one in-person recruitment event per academic year on request, and student contact information including mobile numbers within 30 days (previously 60); Sec. 542 raises the Junior ROTC unit range in 10 U.S.C. 2031(i) from 3,400 to 4,000 to 3,600 to 4,200, effective 2027-10-01, and repeals the FY2025 NDAA change to 3,500 to 4,100 before it took effect.

title: Expand recruiter access to schools, universal ASVAB and Junior ROTC units
uncertainties: The enrolled text of P.L. 119-60 on govinfo.gov (HTML and PDF) could be read only as far as the end of the table of contents, so the terms of Sec. 531 and Sec. 542 rest on the U.S. Code amendment notes on law.cornell.edu (10 U.S.C. 503 and 2031) and on an earlier copy supplied to the project; both report that neither section mentions the ASVAB. Sec. 531 differs from S. 3052 as introduced on the number of required events (one per year against four), and the notes give no separate effective date for Sec. 531. Sec. 542 changes the range that existed before the review period (3,400 to 4,000) to 3,600 to 4,200 effective 2027-10-01, so that increase was enacted within the review period but is not yet operative; per the 10 U.S.C. 2031 notes, Sec. 542(c) repealed the FY2025 NDAA change to 3,500 to 4,100 (set for 2026-10-01), so the range CRS describes never took effect. The equal campus-access requirement in 20 U.S.C. 7908a was enacted before the review period (2024-12-23) and took effect 2025-12-23. The Wicker release gives no unit numbers or section. Sec. 534, on Armed Forces Qualification Test scores for a preparatory course, is not an ASVAB requirement for students and was not treated as one. Actual unit counts after FY2025 were not found.
